burton_span.exact: I had rather drown you, than you should drown me

2.3.3.1-f166.text: abite nummi, ego vos mergam, ne mergar a vobis

translations.note: Burton's English that follows renders only the second clause; it leaves out the opening dismissal 'abite nummi'. The story of Crates throwing his money into the sea is told by several ancient and later writers. Burton names no source for this Latin wording, and the sidenote 'In frag.' belongs to the Cotta speech from Sallust that comes next.

burton_span.exact: I had rather drown you, than you should drown me

translations.text: Away with you, coins! I will drown you, so that I am not drowned by you.

translations.note: The saying attributed to Crates of Thebes; the sidenote 'In frag.' is not clearly attached to this phrase. Burton's English follows immediately.
